global_organization_chain: translate three bat-performance questions into BBS and controllability outputs
state assumptions, geometry, and collision notation
locate the BBS-maximizing impact point analytically and by simulation
augment the baseline with double-spring restitution and empirical swing coupling
map corking geometry and filler properties to mass, inertia, stiffness, and BBS
construct a matched metal-bat comparator to isolate material and trampoline effects
convert modeled performance differences into safety, fairness, and design consequences
stress the main decisions through one-factor sweeps and external curves
close the three questions in their original order and retain derivations and plotting code in appendices

main_argument_chains.claim: The sweet spot can be operationalized as the impact location that maximizes batted-ball speed under the collision model.
support_steps: derive BBS from momentum, angular momentum, and restitution
reduce the expression with stated approximations
differentiate with respect to impact location
check the location across pitch and swing inputs
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Report an interior location about 15 cm from the bat end for the stated baseline rather than treating the tip as optimal.

main_argument_chains.claim: Corking changes BBS through competing changes in mass, inertia, swing speed, stiffness, and effective restitution.
support_steps: translate structural changes into collision parameters
represent radial compliance with a double-spring surrogate
sweep hole radius, depth, and filler density
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat corking as a bounded design tradeoff whose net BBS effect depends on material and geometry.

main_argument_chains.claim: A matched metal bat can separate trampoline behavior from gross geometry and inertial differences.
support_steps: hold mass, center of mass, inertia, length, and outer shape fixed
show that a feasible aluminum design exists
check the direction against an external example
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Attribute the residual modeled performance difference to the material/compliance branch within the matched comparison.

main_argument_chains.claim: The main impact-location decision is stable under the tested inputs and compatible with cited response curves.
support_steps: vary pitch, linear swing, and angular swing inputs
compare the same BBS-versus-location response with external data
inspect paired vibration-energy and effective-restitution plots
quantify the omitted vibration contribution near the decision region
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain the concise baseline for the tested decision region while keeping vibration and empirical-coupling limits explicit.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: A collision schematic defines velocity directions, angles, impact location, bat geometry, and center of mass before the governing equations.
The BBS-versus-impact-location curve directly annotates the interior optimum and the bat tip, converting the central claim into a visible comparison.
A three-dimensional surface with projected contours maps two design variables to maximum BBS and labels the uncorked baseline.
A labeled contour chart provides more readable iso-BBS regions and complements the 3D surface.
A three-column logic diagram links bat type through mechanical variables to controllability and BBS.
Paired impact-location plots show vibration energy minimized and effective restitution maximized in the same region used to defend the simplified model.
